extracted.intended_audience: policymakers, reform-minded readers, and general readers interested in land taxation and social/economic reform
extracted.subtask_description: Argument and practical principles for shifting all public taxation onto the unimproved value of land (land-rent), describing economic, distributional, social, and administrative effects and defending the policy against common objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place all public taxes on the value (rent) of land
rubrics_metrics.description: The state should shift the burden of taxation from production and exchange to the value or rent of land — placing all taxes on land value while leaving labor and capital free of taxation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This single tax on land values would effectively 'put up the land at auction' to the highest rent-payer (the state). It should apply to all land (agricultural, mineral, urban), consume nearly the value of rent preventing holding land without using it, and replace taxes on improvements, machinery, stock, and commodities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exempt labor, capital, and improvements from taxation
rubrics_metrics.description: Labor and capital are to be left their full reward; taxation should not be levied on improvements, machinery, or personal property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By taxing only bare land value, persons who build houses, plant orchards, erect manufactories, or invest in machinery would pay no more in taxes than if the land were idle. This removes the current tax-as-a-fine-on-improvement effect and stimulates investment and improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use land-rent revenues for public benefits (equal distribution of communal gain)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rent taken by the community for public purposes should be applied to public benefits so that increasing rent accrues to every member of the community rather than private landowners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collecting the full rent and applying it to common uses turns rent from a cause of inequality into a source promoting equality (public amenities, services, and benefits accessible to all).

rubrics_metrics.name: Destroy land speculation and monopolization by taxing speculative rent away
rubrics_metrics.description: A land-value tax would make landholding without use unprofitable, causing selling prices to fall and ending land speculation and monopolization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High speculative values would be abandoned or sold on nominal terms, opening up millions of acres to settlers and productive use; urban vacant lots would be brought into their most profitable use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open natural opportunities and expand access to land (accessibility criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Taxing land values removes the barrier that forces laborers to buy or mortgage themselves into land, allowing willing men to become their own employers and freeing access to land for cultivation and homesteads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lower land prices and the absence of speculative premiums make land affordable for farmers and builders, spreading settlement and enabling labor to turn into self-employment where desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve labor market dynamics: employers compete for labor
rubrics_metrics.description: With land freely available for use, employers would have to compete with laborers who could become their own employers, driving wages up to fair earnings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labor would no longer have to underbid each other for employment; the demand of labor itself (its ability to become independent) acts as a countervailing competitor, raising wage levels and reducing involuntary unemployment and paroxysms that paralyze industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase efficiency and productivity by raising habitual wages
rubrics_metrics.description: Higher wages improve the efficiency of labor, encouraging invention and the adoption of labor-saving processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poorly paid labor is less productive; increased wages mean increased self-respect, intelligence, hope and energy, which harness mental faculties to production and accelerate innovation and diffusion of machinery as a blessing rather than a curse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redistribute gains from material progress to public benefit rather than private rent
rubrics_metrics.description: As productive power increases with progress, the increment that would otherwise accrue as increased rent should be captured by the community and used for common benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If rent is taxed away, future increases in productivity enlarge public revenues and public benefits rather than entrenching private wealth; this enables broad improvement in condition for all classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce waste and social costs caused by unequal distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriation of rent to public purposes would remove many economic wastes stemming from poverty, vice, and misdirected private effort to attain wealth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Savings include reduced public charity expenditures, recovered potential earnings of wasted labor, lower crime-related costs, and improved public morality and governance resulting from less inequality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favor working farmers and homestead owners (distributional impact on small owners)
rubrics_metrics.description: Small farmers and homestead owners, who are both laborers and capitalists, would generally gain because land taxation would not penalize improvements and would relieve them of many current taxation burdens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the market selling value of their lots may fall, their useful possession remains; they benefit from exemption of improvements and from higher wages, reduced commodity taxes, and lower speculative land values that enable better settled rural communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: No compensation necessary for existing landholders (justification against compensation claim)
rubrics_metrics.description: Current landholders have no just claim to compensation when the community takes rent through taxation because the value they claim is a social product, and even without compensation they will not be truly injured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large landowners may lose relative income but retain buildings, personal property and productive assets; overall gains in production and wages mean absolute gains for most, and the policy 'impoverishes no one' in a meaningful sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplify government administration by consolidating revenue sources
rubrics_metrics.description: A single tax on land values would vastly simplify tax collection, reduce the machinery needed to collect diverse taxes, and shrink the administrative burden of government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Much of governmental business now devoted to preventing evasion and checking revenues would vanish; administrative and compliance costs would fall dramatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce legal disputes and criminality tied to land ownership and poverty
rubrics_metrics.description: State appropriation of land-rent would diminish civil litigation over land ownership and reduce criminality bred by want, leading to reduced need for courts, police, prisons and many lawyers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If occupiers become practical tenants with rent paid to the community, land-related disputes fall; improved social conditions from higher wages and reduced poverty reduce crime and related public costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enable and fund public works, services, and cultural institutions from land-rent revenue
rubrics_metrics.description: The surplus revenue from land values could be applied to public infrastructure and amenities—telegraph, railroads, water, heat, lighting, museums, libraries, schools, public baths, play grounds, and incentives for discovery and science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With simplified and reduced former expenditures, government could assume constructive services without strain and enhance public life and opportunity for all.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge that equalization is not enforced uniformity of wealth
rubrics_metrics.description: Equal distribution under land-value taxation does not mean everyone receives identical wealth; remaining inequalities would reflect natural differences in ability and desire, not artificial monopolies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The policy aims that wealth be distributed according to each person's contribution of industry, skill, knowledge, or prudence, removing rents that result from denying natural opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept loss of extreme wealth-accumulation incentives as socially tolerable
rubrics_metrics.description: Removing the incentive to pursue great wealth for its own sake is a desirable outcome because fear of want is the root of excessive greed and many social ills; reduced appetite for extravagant accumulation need not harm production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The motivation to produce driven by fear of poverty can be spared; intellectual and socially higher pursuits will absorb energies formerly squandered on accumulating riches at social cost.
